messages:
Devon: Heads-up — eviction spikes for preemptible GPU pools in us-west2 over the last 72h. p95 eviction rate jumped from ~9% -> ~27% during peak windows. Thinking we should try a graded-bid mix + soft-eviction buffer to smooth oscillation. Anyone seeing different data?
Sean: Can you paste the dashboard numbers? which instance types and zones?
Devon: Quick snapshot: GPU G7x + A10x pools. evictions clustered in us-west2-a/b, median lifetime down from 4h -> 1.2h. Cost if we switch fully to capacity-optimized would be ~+8% but p99 tail latency drops.
Nina: Also saw higher egress spikes to our analytics cluster in us-west2 on those nodes — might be network congestion making scheduler slow to restart. Might exacerbate apparent evictions (pods OOM/terminated while transient network blips).
CapacityBot: ALERT: preemptible-eviction-rate > 20% for pool=gpu-a10x-us-west2 in 3h window (1754319000 - 1754320800). Suggested action: reduce price-optimized weight or increase warm-buffer.
Lia: Proposal: run a 48h experiment with "graded bidding" (70% capacity-optimized, 30% price-optimized) + soft-eviction TTL and a 10% warm buffer per zone. If evictions still >18% we failover to us-west1 on a per-slot basis.
Sean: +1. We should also enable a short prefix KV caching on restart to avoid cold-KV pressure while nodes spin up.
Devon: Agreed. Draft config for procurement controller (example):
```yaml
procurement_policy:
  pools:
    - name: gpu-primary
      weight_capacity_optimized: 70
      weight_price_optimized: 30
      warm_buffer_percent: 10
      soft_eviction_ttl_secs: 300  # give 5m to gracefully drain
    - name: gpu-fallback
      regions: [us-west1]
      weight_capacity_optimized: 100
```
Lia: The soft_eviction_ttl helps because our graceful shutdown hooks can flush KV/onnx caches. If TTL too low we lose state and spiky retries hit the API.
Nina: For networking, I recommend steering heavier workloads to AZs with direct peering to analytics (us-west2-b has better path). We'll include a routing affinity in the rollout.
ops-oncall: Can we get a pager rule for when eviction-rate > 25% AND warm_buffer_utilization > 80%? We nearly got paged last night.
Devon: Yes — creating rule now. Also scheduling a canary: 100 GPUs in graded mix for 6h, measure p95 latency and cost-per-token. If p95 drops and eviction <18% we roll to 60% of fleet.
Sean: How do we measure oscillation? Metric idea: eviction-rate-derivative (evictions/min change) + pool-swap-rate. If derivative > threshold, throttle rebalances for 10m.
Lia: Exactly — add hysteresis to the controller: require 3 consecutive 5m windows before changing major weights. That avoids oscillatory flip-flop.
Devon: I'll push the procurement change to staging and kick off the canary tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Ownership: Devon + Lia. ops-oncall will monitor.
Nina: I'll adjust routing affinity and check peering counters. If we see packet drops >0.5% we abort and fall back to us-west1.
CapacityBot: NOTE: procurement change deployed to staging by Devon at 1754322200. Canary scheduled for 1754325600.
ops-oncall: Thanks — ping here when canary starts, will watch dashboards and reserve on-call for the window. :thumbsup:
Devon: Thanks all, we'll reconvene after canary with results + a short runbook update for evictions. :rocket:
